decisions.reason: As a very new but strategically relevant particle-therapy product, management would likely keep it because there is no clear evidence yet of performance below aspiration, though its niche market and delayed US availability raise uncertainty.
This chamber sits close to the firm’s core dosimetry capabilities, so with no sign of disappointing results and with likely slack from the established business, management would keep it.

Because it is another core-category dosimetry product and there is no observed shortfall versus aspirations, the firm would be inclined to continue offering it rather than trigger problemistic search.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line with several models fits routine customer demand and the firm’s existing strengths, making it unlikely to be withdrawn so soon after launch.
Relative dosimetry is central to the firm’s offering, so absent evidence of underperformance management would likely keep the product while learning about adoption in the market.
The thimble ionization chamber is a conventional adjacent product for this specialised portfolio, and early-stage uncertainty alone would usually not justify dropping it within a year.
